newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore opposition party plans to soldier on.
newsitem.headline: Singapore opposition party plans to soldier on.

text.p: Singapore's main opposition party said it faced a serious financial setback but would continue to speak up after a parliamentary committee recommended that its leaders be fined for acting in contempt of parliament.
Chee Soon Juan, secretary-general of the Singapore Democratic Party (SDP), said in a statement late on Friday: "We will stomach this blow and struggle on. Our duty to Singaporeans remains steadfast."
The committee of privileges recommended in a report on Friday that parliament fine Chee Singapore $25,000 (US$17,900) and that three other SDP leaders receive fines ranging from S$5,000 to S$13,000.

The committee found that Chee, who has the highest profile in the SDP, had fabricated data and falsified documents presented to a select committee on health care and subsequently misled the committee when challenged over the figures.
The others were found in contempt.
Chee told the committee the figure was a typing mistake and a result of human error.
He said in the statement the SDP had highlighted Singaporeans' concerns over health care subsidies to the government throughout the hearing on the issue.
"As a result, many more questions have been raised which will be brought to the attention of Singaporeans at the coming general election," he said.
Chee and the others could be barred from contesting future elections if the case were passed on to a civil court which then found against them.
But if parliament follows the committee recommendations, that should leave the four free to run in the general election Singapore must hold by April. Chee is widely expected to do so.
